You are a hazard to the road. Speed limits are suggestions in most cases. You only have to follow them in adverse weather or when the law is around.

In theory if the speed limit is 45 you can get a ticket for going 46 even if road conditions are ideal. They usually aren't so strictly enforced, you can go slightly above and probably not get pulled over, but that is how speed limits technically work. Also legally if the speed limit is 45, I'm going 43, I get rear ended by the person behind me going 53 than the driver who rear ended me would be at fault for it and would have to pay the damages. But I can't get a ticket for going 43 in the 45 zone though you can at least in theory get a ticket for going even 46.

Common radar guns have +/- 1 MPH accuracy, so you will almost never have a speeding citation stick if you were only clocked one MPH over the limit. Regardless though, this is why I stated that you need only follow the limit when an officer is around to stop you.

As for getting rear ended by someone going 53, good luck proving what speed they were going. You won't get a ticket for going 2 MPH under, but 10+ under might get you a ticket for driving at an unsafe speed.

How big is your hands? Are you a 90 pound woman or a 260 lb man? There is no 'right 'answer to this, it's whatever you are comfortable shooting and can put hits on target with. I did this not too long ago.

  1. Sign up for First Shots. It's free, (well like $20) and you will get a brief safety course and shoot a revolver and a semi auto .22 cal. I went with my wife, we both had an awesome time. http://www.nssf.org/firstshots/

  2. Use that $20 coupon and go to the range with a friend whose also interested in learning to shoot. Try out at least a compact, a full-size semi-auto and a revolver. You're gonna want to walk away from this knowing the difference between .38, 9mm and .45 as well as the difference between single action, double action only and single/double action.

  3. Do a bunch of internet research. Figure out your budge. The new Walther Creed is ~$400, so look for something around that price. Plan on buying new so you get the warranty.

  4. Go to gun store, try out grips, rack the slide, check the sites, dry fire the pistol to get a feel for the trigger action, go with the one that "just feels right". For example I went with a Springfield Armory XD Mod 2 5" Tactical. This is large enough for my smaller wife to shoot reliably (the larger and heavier the pistol, the LESS recoil usually), fits my hand really well, shoots super straight and is comfortable to use all day at the range (if you're not going to the range, you're missing like 90% of the point of owning a pistol), and will perform fantastic as home defense and most important, my wife knows how to use it and has practiced using it.

Pistol? Glock, or Ruger Mark IV. But pistols are VERY limited in effectiveness for numberous reasons. For actual utility in a SHTF situation .22 rifle like a Ruger 10/22, or better yet, a pump action 12 gauge is WAY better.

Lots of sound advice here but there's something you need to consider: How common is it to get bullets?

Your most common sizes are 22, 357, 9, 45, 38.

A 357 can shoot 38s. That has the most versatility.

22s are always in high demand. They are cheap so a lot of people have 22 guns. If you're looking at a potential ammo shortage, 22s are going to be gone quickly.

And judging by how everyone likes 9 mm guns, those will be gone quickly too.

45s are kind of common as well.

Personally, I'd go with a little guy that you can hide very easily (my choice is a 25) and then a 357. The 25 is hidden and for "I have nothing else" and the 357 is... yeah, it's a 357.

If you're talking long guns, you probably want to stick with shotgun or 22. There's a 22 that I saw a video of where the bullet is slowed down to subsonic speeds and it has pretty much no report.
